resources.title: Secondary Education Curriculum 2076 — Physics, Grades 11 & 12 (Subject code Phy-101 / Phy-102, 5 credit hrs, 160 working hrs)
resources.accessNote: Official but geo-slow — CDC's e-library server is very slow / often times out from outside Nepal. Retry, or reach it via the portal below.
resources.why: The single most important document at this level. NePhO Round 1 is explicitly based on it.

resources.title: Curriculum Development Centre (CDC) — Digital Library portal
resources.accessNote: Same geo-slowness. Accessible from within Nepal.
resources.why: Entry point for all NEB textbooks & curricula.

resources.title: OpenStax , Vol. 1 (Mechanics)
resources.why: Calculus-based, IPhO-grade rigour, legally free, and it is the direct upgrade path from the NEB textbook. Prabhakar Kafle (IPhO 2017 bronze) recommends "University Physics" as the top choice for students comfortable with calculus.

resources.title: OpenStax , Vol. 2 (Thermodynamics, E&M, Optics)
resources.why: Covers the entire NePhO Round-2 optics + induction + AC gap.

resources.title: OpenStax , Vol. 3 (Modern & Quantum Physics)
resources.why: Photons, matter waves, uncertainty principle, nuclear — the Final-Round modern-physics syllabus.

resources.title: HyperPhysics (Georgia State University)
resources.why: Fast concept cross-referencing; excellent for filling holes before you touch olympiad problems.

resources.title: Graphing for NePhO — Prabhakar Kafle & Sanam Limbu
resources.why: Explicitly built for NePhO. Opens with a NePhO Pre-selection 2017 graph question. Graphing is a named scoring skill in the official NePhO syllabus. 5 pp.

resources.title: Significant Figures and Rounding — Kafle & Limbu
resources.why: NePhO papers state: "Marks will not be deducted for incorrect answers but deducted for improper significant figures." This is free marks most Nepali students lose. 2 pp.

resources.title: Errors and their Propagation — Kafle & Limbu
resources.why: Foundation for the mandatory "Experimental uncertainty & Data analysis" syllabus section. 4 pp.

resources.title: Uncertainty and Error Propagation — V. Lindberg (LSU/RIT)
resources.why: The quick version. Recommended by IPhO-2017 medallists specifically for NePhO-only preparation.

resources.title: MIT OCW 8.01SC Classical Mechanics
resources.why: Full first-year mechanics with problem sets + exams. The standard bridge from board physics to olympiad mechanics.

resources.title: The Feynman Lectures on Physics (Vol. I / II / III + Tips on Physics)
resources.accessNote: LIVE but bot-walled (returns 403 to scripts/scrapers — opens fine in a normal browser)
resources.why: Legal free HTML edition from Caltech. Kafle's advice: "like physics, but don't enjoy reading course books? Have a look at Feynman." Read-only online (downloads not permitted).

resources.title: A Guide to Nepal Physics Olympiad
resources.why: Written by Laxman Bist, Nabin Kalauni, Sandesh Parajuli — top-3 of NePhO 2018, Nepal's team at IPhO 2018 Lisbon. Explicitly "organized as per the syllabus of NePhO." Every chapter = Key Concepts & Formulae → Bridging Problem → Level 1 problems → Level 2 problems → IPhO problems → Supplementary problems, all with solutions. Sources cited inside: Morin, Irodov, Gnädig, Sears & Zemansky. Released Oct 2023, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

resources.title: Mechanics for NePhO — Dinesh Kandel (IPhO 2011 Bronze, Nepal)
resources.why: "Preparation Materials FOR IPhO — NePhO, Nepal Physical Society." Contains an actual NePhO 2011 selection-test problem (falling-raindrop model) worked up to competition standard. The deepest Nepal-authored mechanics treatment available.

resources.title: An Introduction to Error Analysis — John R. Taylor
resources.accessNote: Unreachable from some networks (India-hosted mirror; times out abroad). Search title to find it; or buy.
resources.why: Kafle: "if you want in-depth knowledge from the very beginning (which will be required eventually in IPhO), the best material should be John R. Taylor's." The definitive text.

resources.title: BdPhO Past Papers — 13th BdPhO, Category C (Higher Secondary)
resources.accessNote: LIVE but JavaScript-only SPA — needs a browser; not scrapeable. Category A/B/C correspond to school tiers.
resources.why: Bangladesh's olympiad has an identical ladder shape to what you want: Selection Round → Regional Round (multiple question sets) → National Round, with Category C = higher secondary = Nepal's Grade 11–12. Difficulty sits right between NePhO Round 1 and Round 2. The single best volume-drill source for South Asian students.

resources.title: HBCSE (India) — Past Papers index (NSEP + INPhO, 2008–2025, English and Hindi)
resources.accessNote: Index ✅ LIVE, but individual PDFs 404 from non-Indian IPs (geo-restricted). Use from within Nepal/India or via archive.org.
resources.why: India's national olympiad papers with official model solutions. INPhO is ~1 notch above NePhO Final Round; NSEP is ~NePhO Round 1. Hindi versions help Nepali students more comfortable in Devanagari.

resources.title: MIT OCW 8.02 Physics II — Electricity & Magnetism
resources.why: Covers magnetic field, magnetic properties of materials, electromagnetic induction, alternating currents — the entire §2 of the official Final-Selection syllabus, which no Nepali resource covers.

resources.title: MIT OCW 8.03SC Physics III — Vibrations and Waves
resources.why: Covers mechanical waves, acoustic phenomena, interference, diffraction, polarization — the entire §1 of the official Final-Selection syllabus, also uncovered by Nepali material.

resources.title: BdPhO National Round papers, Category C
resources.why: The National Round of BdPhO ≈ NePhO Final Round in difficulty and is freely downloadable (unlike INPhO).

resources.title: Jaan Kalda — study guide (ver 0.87)
resources.why: IPhO-level thermodynamics with hints. Bridges NePhO Round 1 thermo → Round 2 → IPhO.

resources.title: Jaan Kalda — (ver 1.2)
resources.why: DC/AC circuit theory at olympiad depth — covers the Kirchhoff / thermoelectric / AC circuits syllabus items the Nepal guide omits.

resources.title: Jaan Kalda — (ver 0.5)
resources.why: Interference, diffraction, polarization. The only free olympiad-grade optics handout identified; there is no Nepali equivalent at any level.

resources.title: Jaan Kalda — (ver 1.2)
resources.why: Rotation, rigid bodies, gravitation, oscillations — the Round-1 mechanics blocks missing from the Nepal guide.

resources.title: Jaan Kalda — "Recommended list of problems"
resources.why: The most respected curated olympiad problem list in the world, hand-picked by an IPhO organiser and sorted by topic: Mechanics (incl. celestial), Electromagnetism, Thermodynamics, Optics, Relativity, Quantum. Each entry annotated with why it teaches something (e.g. "IPhO-1991-Pr1 — this will teach you the basics of the collision of bodies"). Start here before touching raw archives.

resources.title: Physics Cup (by mail, IPhO Estonia) — open online competition, problems 2012 → 2020
resources.why: Low-stakes, monthly, solution-published. Ideal for building consistency between NePhO rounds.

resources.title: Nordic-Baltic Physics Olympiad (NBPhO) problems
resources.why: Kalda's own regional olympiad; the Est-Fin problems on his recommended list come from here.

resources.title: Gulf Physics Olympiads (GPhO)
resources.why: ABEGS-organised; 3 editions with problems.

resources.title: AAPT — U.S. Physics Team exams (F=ma, USAPhO, USAPhO Plus), all years + solutions
resources.why: F=ma is a 25-question/75-min MCQ round — perfect timed-drill material for NePhO Section A; USAPhO is free-response at NePhO-Final/IPhO difficulty.

resources.title: Official IPhO Syllabus (accepted Astana 2014, amended Mumbai 2015)
resources.why: Section-by-section: 2.2 Mechanics (kinematics / statics / dynamics / celestial mechanics), 2.3 Electromagnetic fields (basic concepts / integral forms of Maxwell's equations / interaction of matter with fields / circuits), 2.4 Oscillations & waves (single oscillator / waves / interference & diffraction / EM waves in matter), plus thermodynamics, modern physics, and experimental skills incl. error analysis.

resources.title: Kalda — "Formulas for IPhO" (ver 1.1)
resources.why: The de-facto standard IPhO formula sheet. Also in Spanish, Japanese, Portuguese, Indonesian, Estonian — no Nepali version exists (Gap I-3).

Kalda — Theory of Relativity (Siim Ainsaar, ver 0.6)

resources.title: Physoly — Lagrangian formalism handout (Ashmit Dutta)
resources.why: Lagrangian methods unlock a large class of IPhO mechanics problems with far less algebra. Not in any syllabus but heavily rewarded.

resources.title: Physoly — Parabolic Projectiles (Ahmed Saad Sabit)
resources.why: Directrix/focus methods for hard projectile problems. Maps onto NePhO 2022-style QN6(A).

resources.title: Physoly — Maxwellian Distribution (Murad Bashirov)
resources.why: Kinetic theory at olympiad depth (NePhO syllabus: "kinetic theory of gases and gas laws").

resources.title: Physoly — "Golden Ratio" problem collection (QiLin Xue)
resources.why: Dozens of worked problems from Morin, Purcell, Kalda, PhysicsBrawl, Pathfinder whose answer is φ. Excellent pattern-recognition drill.

resources.title: Physoly Mock F=ma 2020 + Solutions
resources.why: Timed MCQ mock in the exact NePhO Section-A / F=ma style.

resources.title: Physoly Mock F=ma 2021 + Solutions
Physoly Mock F=ma 2022 + Solutions

gaps.missing: ⭐ EXPERIMENTAL PHYSICS TRAINING MANUAL FOR NEPAL. NPS's 2025/26 notice confirms the Final Round includes an experimental examination. There is no Nepali experimental olympiad material of any kind — not in the NPS documents, not in *A Guide to Nepal Physics Olympiad* (0 pages of lab content), not on any Nepali site.
gaps.evidence: This is the largest single gap in Nepali physics-olympiad preparation. IPhO allocates 20 of 50 marks to experiment. Nepal's whole medal record rests on theory performance alone.
gaps.aiSpec: Generate "NePhO/IPhO Experimental Physics Manual for Nepal" in 4 parts: (1) Apparatus literacy — vernier caliper, screw gauge, stopwatch, spring balance, metre scale, multimeter, galvanometer, potentiometer, travelling microscope, optical bench, spherometer, sonometer, calorimeter, thermistor, photogate; least count and zero-error for each. (2) 40 standard experiments with objective, apparatus, procedure, observation table, sample data, graph to plot, uncertainty budget, and result — chosen from NEB Gr. 11/12 practicals *plus* IPhO/EuPhO experimental tasks (pendulum & g, moment of inertia by torsion, Young's modulus by Searle, focal length by u–v and by displacement method, refractive index of prism, metre bridge & potentiometer, EMF/internal resistance, diode & Zener characteristics, transistor gain, half-life by GM counter / simulation, Stefan–Boltzmann, Wien, specific heat, surface tension by capillary, viscosity by Stokes, speed of sound by resonance column, solar-cell I–V, LC oscillations, coefficient of restitution). (3) Data analysis — random vs systematic, absolute/relative uncertainty, addition by modulus vs Pythagorean, standard deviation, linearisation of nonlinear relations, least-squares fit with uncertainties on slope and intercept, optimal graph scales, error bars, residual plots. (4) Low-cost / at-home substitutes — because most district schools in Nepal lack the apparatus; specify phone-sensor (phyphox), ruler-and-string, and simulation (PhET) alternatives for every experiment.
